name: Question 20
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{5}-8,2{t}^{4}-6⟩,$ $t\in (0,\infty )$, find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{5}-8),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-6)⟩ \\  & =⟨5{t}^{4},8{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\ ⟨5{t}^{4},8{t}^{3}⟩ & =c⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\ ⟨5{t}^{4},8{t}^{3}⟩ & =⟨c,\frac{4c}{5}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{t}^{4}=c \\ 8{t}^{3}=\frac{4c}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $c=5{t}^{4}.$ Substituting $c=5{t}^{4}$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{t}^{3} & =\frac{4(5{t}^{4})}{5} \\ 8{t}^{3}-4{t}^{4} & =0 \\ 4{t}^{3}(2-t) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=2.$ 

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =⟨(2)^{5}-8,2(2)^{4}-6⟩=⟨24,26⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(24,26).$

Question 20
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨t5−8,2t4−6⟩, t∈(0,∞), find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector ⟨1,45⟩.

a
 (−9,−4) and (−8,−6)
b
 (−9,−4)
c
 (24,26)
d
 (−7,−4)
e
 (−7,−4) and (24,26)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(t5−8),ddt(2t4−6)⟩=⟨5t4,8t3⟩

The vectors r′(t) and ⟨1,45⟩ are parallel for some specific value t0 of the parameter t if and only if there exists a constant c such that r′(t0)=c⟨1,45⟩. So, we have

r′(t)=c⟨1,45⟩⟨5t4,8t3⟩=c⟨1,45⟩⟨5t4,8t3⟩=⟨c,4c5⟩.

Equating the components gives: {5t4=c8t3=4c5

From the first equation, we obtain that c=5t4. Substituting c=5t4 into the second equation, we get 8t3=4(5t4)58t3−4t4=04t3(2−t)=0.

Since t∈(0,∞), the only solution is t=2.

Finally, since r(2)=⟨(2)5−8,2(2)4−6⟩=⟨24,26⟩, we conclude that ⟨1,45⟩ and r′(t) are parallel at the point (24,26).
